newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle market active at $71 - trade.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle market active at $71 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle near midday Wednesday were actively trading at $71.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.

About 20,000 head had been sold in Kansas by late morning and about 22,000 in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma region, but actual totals will likely be larger by the end of the day, cattle feeders said.
However, there were reports that some feedlots were passing packer bids at $71.00 and looking for $72.00 instead, some sources said.
For every feedlot selling cattle at $71.00 there appeared to be another feedlot passing on the bids, the sources said.
Feedlot cattle prices were supported by tight supplies of fed cattle following Friday's active sales and by this week's advances in boxed beef values, they said.

Beef prices, which rose another $0.95 to $1.09 per cwt Tuesday, according to USDA, were supported by strong retail demand for planned promotions at the end. Retailers are expected to feature beef before shifting to pork in October when National Pork Month promotions begin, market sources said.
